notes: Microsoft publishes the full Graph v1.0 surface as an OpenAPI 3.0 document (generated from their CSDL metadata by their own tooling, not by us) at microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata, which makes this found-openapi, not converted. The verbatim upstream (upstream.yaml, 45 MB, hash-locked) is 18,004 operations / 11,632 paths / 5,341 schemas across every Microsoft 365 workload (Teams, SharePoint, Intune device management, security & compliance, identity governance, education, print, ...). openapi.json serves a curated coverage:subset derived mechanically from that file (a filter script, not hand-authored): every path whose top-level resource is one a Graph integration realistically reaches (users, groups, sites, drives/driveItems, applications, servicePrincipals, organization, directory objects/roles, domains, invitations, teams/teamwork/chats, planner, contacts), restricted to at most 5 path segments (entity plus one or two levels of relationship/action), plus the bare /me singleton (the signed-in user, which the mock/adaptor address directly rather than through /users/{id}). That keeps single-hop operations like a driveItem's /content or /createUploadSession while dropping Graph's deep, rarely-used relationship chains (nested OneNote pages, analytics-of-analytics, etc.). Every path/parameter/schema kept is copied byte-for-byte from Microsoft's document (1,775 paths, 2,668 operations, 1,106 schemas) via a transitive $ref closure, not re-authored, so completeness is 'complete' rather than best-effort. Verified against ast.json: the adaptor's 6 HTTP operations (create, get, getDrive, getFolder, getFile, uploadFile) are all generic builders with no fixed path, and every endpoint their docs/source name as an example (/drives/{id}, /drives/{id}/items/{id}/children, /drives/{id}/items/{id}/content, /drives/{id}/items/{id}/createUploadSession, /sites/{id}/drive, /groups/{id}/drive, /applications) is present in the subset. Previously this adaptor's spec was a ~17-endpoint hand-picked stub, the exact 'focused subset' anti-pattern AGENTS.md warns against; this replaces it with a real vendor document narrowed by a documented, mechanical rule instead of by guessing at adaptor usage. Left out: Intune/device management, security & compliance, identity governance, education, print, reports, and most of onenote/todo/presence, all real Graph resources the adaptor's generic builders could reach but that no realistic OpenFn workflow targets; a future pass could widen the depth/tag allowlist if that changes. The filter script is not in the repo, so its exact rule is recorded here for the next refresh (re-implemented on 2026-11-16 and proven to reproduce the previous openapi.json byte-for-byte from the previous upstream.yaml before being applied to the new one): parse upstream.yaml with the `yaml` package; keep a path when its first segment is exactly one of users, groups, sites, drives, applications, servicePrincipals, organization, directory, directoryObjects, directoryRoles, domains, invitations, teams, teamwork, chats, planner, contacts (so alternate-key roots such as /users(userPrincipalName='{userPrincipalName}') are not kept) and it has at most 5 segments, in upstream order, then append /me last; collect #/components/* $refs breadth-first in discovery order (paths first, then each referenced component in turn) and emit components as schemas, parameters, responses, requestBodies in that discovery order; copy openapi, servers and the full tags list from upstream; info is upstream's with the curated title plus x-openfn-adaptor and x-openfn-subset-note; write with JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2) and a trailing newline. Upstream drift re-captured 2026-11-16 (Microsoft's file grew by 139 paths / 227 operations / 214 schemas): the subset gained 38 paths / 63 operations / 50 schemas and lost none - chiefly the new /directory/tenantGovernance tree (45 operations), /users/{id}/notes (11), /users/{id}/authentication/resourceAccountKeyAuthenticationMethods (4), /users/{id}/calendars/delta(), /drives/{id}/list/subscriptions/getVapidPublicKey() and /sites/{id}/permissions/{id}/revokeGrants - with 2 operations and 25 schemas changed in place.
